sheet.content:
## Key definitions
- **Transport layer**: Provides process-to-process delivery [p. 1]
- **Port numbers**: 16-bit number (0 to 65535) identifying a process on a host [p. 1]
- **Socket**: Combination of an IP address and a port number [p. 1]
- **UDP**: Connectionless, unreliable transport protocol with very little overhead [p. 2]
- **TCP**: Connection-oriented and reliable, numbers every byte [p. 2]
- **DNS**: Maps host names to IP addresses [p. 2]
- **HTTP**: Application layer protocol for web communication [p. 2]
- **FTP**: Application layer protocol for file transfer [p. 2]
- **SMTP**: Application layer protocol for email [p. 2]

## Diagrams to draw
- **UDP and TCP Sockets**: Sockets address combination of IP address and port number [p. 1]

## Formulas and code
None in this unit

## Must remember
- **TCP uses sequence numbers for byte numbering** [p. 2]
- **UDP has a 8-byte header** [p. 2]
- **TCP is reliable, UDP is unreliable** [p. 2]
- **TCP uses acknowledgments and retransmissions** [p. 2]
- **UDP is connectionless and has no flow control** [p. 2]
